summary: Ram Island Light, Boothbay Harbor, Maine: first lit in 1883 on a ledge off Ram Island, automated in 1965, now owned by a museum trust.

access.note: Not open to the public (USLHS). LighthouseFriends says grounds open, tower and dwelling closed; the New England Lighthouses guide says grounds open by appointment.

events.note: Congress appropriates $5,000 for a light on Ram Island (3 March 1837). The Board of Navy Commissioners then recommends suspending the spending.
USLHS gives 1881 as the year the original fourth-order Fresnel lens was installed. LighthouseFriends describes the lens as part of the 1883 station. Unresolved.
Congress approves $25,000 for an official station on 7 August 1882.
Tower and keeper's dwelling built; the NRHP nomination says the complex, except the oil house, was built in 1883.
Lit for the first time 5 November 1883 (LighthouseFriends).
Samuel Cavanor appointed keeper, reported October 1883.
On 1 October 1889 the sectors were reversed: white marks the safe approaches, red warns of danger.
23 November 1891: Keeper Cavanor and keeper James Burke rescue Allen Conary, whose boat sank off Spruce Point near Fisherman's Island.
A thousand-pound fog bell, struck by machinery, is established (report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1897).
Walkway damaged 18 January 1903 when the schooner Harriet W. Babson grounded on the island.
7 July 1939: the Coast Guard takes over the Lighthouse Service.
A modern foghorn replaces the fog bell.
Coast Guard announces it will demolish the keeper's house; the Grand Banks Schooner Museum Trust leases the station.
Ownership of the site granted to the Grand Banks Schooner Museum Trust through the Maine Lights Program; the Coast Guard keeps the active light.

keepers.name: Samuel John Cavanor
keepers.note: Appointed October 1883 (Portland Daily Press). Died 1913. Born in Halifax, Nova Scotia, per the Boothbay Register notice.

keepers.name: O. G. Reed
keepers.note: Captain O. G. Reed took temporary charge (LighthouseFriends). USLHS lists the line as Principal Lighthouse Keeper.

keepers.name: Almon Mitchell
keepers.note: Made keeper 10 May 1913. Died of heart failure in 1925 at 68 (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Ralph C. Norwood
keepers.note: Moved to the station in early 1945 (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Terry E. Stanley
keepers.note: USLHS lists 1965-1965; LighthouseFriends gives an open-ended term (1965 onward). No source says he was on duty at automation.

wrecks.outcome: Grounded on Ram Island while returning from Newfoundland with salt herring. Walkway damaged; light dark for a few nights until the walkway was repaired.
Ran aground on nearby Squirrel Island (keeper's letter of 6 December 1884, as quoted by LighthouseFriends).
Went ashore near Ram Island in 1885 (LighthouseFriends; exact location not given).

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-27 against the cached sources: the LighthouseFriends page, the USLHS place record, the NRHP nomination, the Portland Daily Press of 6 Oct 1883 p. 4, the Daily Kennebec Journal of 24 Nov 1891 p. 1 and 17 Apr 1913 p. 6, and the Light-House Board reports (FY1892, FY1897, FY1901). Most anecdotes (the 1837 appropriation and Smith's report, the McKay private light, the hailstorm, the 1885 boat, the 1898 weight box, the 1903 walkway, the 1939-45 items, the 1972-2002 history, the White Woman legend) come from LighthouseFriends only; the story attributes them to it. The 1883 first-lit date and the 1837/1882 appropriations rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The 1837 appropriation is stated as preceding Smith's report of 2 June 1837 (LighthouseFriends sequence); an earlier draft reversed this. The 1891 rescue is from the Daily Kennebec Journal reprint of the Boothbay Register; the second keeper's station is garbled in the OCR, so the story does not name it. The 1913 obituary's vessel name is garbled in the OCR, so the story does not repeat it. The 'probably no family' line is quoted only through LighthouseFriends (the 12 April 1913 Register article was not read directly), so the story paraphrases it. Printed page numbers: FY1897 p. 42 is confirmed on the OCR page header (entry 48). FY1901 p. 49 is confirmed on the OCR page header. FY1892 is cited by scan page 377; the entry is number 46 and the OCR header near it reads 46, but the corpus marks the printed page unconfirmed, so the story uses the scan page. Lens date conflict (USLHS 1881 installed vs LighthouseFriends 1883 station) is unresolved and stated in the story. Record fields not verified here: characteristic 'Iso W 6s' (lead only, not cited) and range 11 nm. The NRHP listing date 1988 in the record is not verified: the nomination form is dated 1987 by receipt stamp. Same-name stations not used: a Ram Island in the Kennebec River (day beacon) and Ram Island Ledge in Casco Bay. Keeper roster: 15 USLHS lines, copied as printed. Terry E. Stanley is named only as a roster entry (1965); no source says he was on duty at automation, and the story says so. Post-1960 keepers appear only as roster names with published spans and no personal details. No photos mirrored.
